description.purpose: A spoken conversation as ONE cell: a WebSocket surface that takes audio in and gives audio back, and text turns on the topology side. It is the voice sibling of the telegram connector -- the same shape, a different medium: one cell, one credential pair, one wire up and one wire down. Speech recognition and synthesis sit behind traits with two shipped adapters each, so which provider speaks is a param and not a rebuild.
description.use_when: Wherever a topology needs a voice surface in front of something ELSE. Instantiate with add_nodes and wire the CELL -- there is no hive path and no lane inside it to hit. An instance is reached at `/<mount>/` on the colony's one listener (`params.mount`, shipped as `voice`), and that is its only door -- `port` and `bind` were removed in 2.0.0. A second instance takes its own mount through override_params. The outbound edge MUST promote hop.call_id to context, or the spoken answer has no connection to go to.
description.not_in_scope: No telephony and no SIP -- the client brings the audio over a WebSocket and takes it back the same way. No resampling, ever: the rate a provider declares is the rate on the wire, and audio at another rate is refused rather than converted. No screening, no persona, no memory, no answer of its own -- that is the firewall template and whatever agent stands behind it. Not a bot either: this is the wire, and a complete spoken bot is this cell plus something that produces answers.
examples: DIRECTIONS - in: an edge onto the CELL carrying the finished assistant turn; context.session_id selects the connection it is spoken into. out: four lanes on hop.route -- 'turn' (a finished utterance as a user-origin text turn, with turn_id), 'partial' (an interim transcript of the same shape; params.emit_partials ships FALSE, so the lane exists only where a manifest ordered it AND drew the edge that drains it) 'error' (the cell's own failure: empty messages[], hop.error_code plus msg_type 'voice_error') and, since 1.3.0, 'speak_end' (one synthesis is over: empty messages[], hop.speak_id and hop.reason done|cancelled|failed; params.emit_speak_end ships FALSE for the partial lane's reason, and the telephony hive is who orders it). Since 1.4.0 every one of the four carries hop.call_id beside hop.session_id -- the same value under the name a channel addresses it by -- and an answer selects its connection with context.call_id; context.session_id is still read where that key is absent, and its owner is unchanged.

Credentials: params.stt.api_key and params.tts.api_key are ${DEEPGRAM_API_KEY} and ${CARTESIA_API_KEY}, and the two blocks are immutable on the runtime params surface -- rotation means .env plus a restart. The 'echo' STT provider needs neither, and no tts block at all: it is the loop that proves the wire without spending a cent.
The two openai adapters speak to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint through base_url, so a local server can stand in for the hosted one without touching the cell.

ONE door: params.mount (shipped as 'voice') is the name this cell is reached under on the colony's one listener, at /<mount>/ws, /<mount>/info and /<mount>/. A name another cell already holds registers nothing and says so, so a second instance takes its own mount through override_params. A mount that moved takes effect on the next life. Migrating from 1.x: drop params.port and params.bind -- a document that still names one is refused at parse time with the sentence that says so -- and put the colony's listener behind a proxy, which is where the authentication this cell type never does belongs.

DEEPGRAM_API_KEY.because: binds `params.stt.api_key`, written `${DEEPGRAM_API_KEY}` with NO default. Declared and NOT required, and both halves are deliberate. Declared, because a builder should learn this template's environment surface by reading it rather than by watching a boot refuse: with the shipped params and this key unset, the colony does not start -- it stops with `env_var_missing` naming the variable, which is the loud failure a token without a default is FOR. Not required, because `stt.provider` is a param and an instantiation may override the whole block onto `echo` (with `"tts": null` beside it, because `override_params` merges and cannot remove a key). The requirement walk reads the TEMPLATE and never the `override_params` beside it, so requiring the key here would refuse the one configuration that is meant to cost nothing. It carries no value in this tree and never should: the token is the name of a secret, not the secret.

CARTESIA_API_KEY.because: binds `params.tts.api_key`, written `${CARTESIA_API_KEY}` with no default, and declared for exactly the reason above. An `echo` instance drops the block entirely with `"tts": null` and needs no synthesis credential; an instantiation that overrides `tts` onto another provider names that provider's own key instead.
